questions.text:
Consider the following sets, where [latex]n\geq 2[/latex]:

S1: Set of all nxn matrices with entries from the set [latex]\{a, b, c\}[/latex]
S2: Set of all functions from the set[latex]\{0,1,2,...,n^2-1\}[/latex] to the set [latex]\{0, 1, 2 \}[/latex]

Which of the following choice(s) is/are correct?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]|S_1|=3^{n^2}[/latex] (each of the [latex]n^2[/latex] entries has 3 choices).
- [latex]|S_2|=3^{n^2}[/latex] (each of the [latex]n^2[/latex] inputs has 3 choices).

Equal finite sizes [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] a bijection exists (read the matrix entries in order as the function values). A bijection is also a surjection and an injection.

Answer: A surjection exists; a bijection exists

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: There does not exist a bijection from S1 to S2
There exists a surjection from S1 to S2
There exists a bijection from S1 to S2
There does not exist an injection from S1 to S2

questions.text: Let [latex]L_1[/latex] be a regular language and [latex]L_2[/latex] be a context-free language. Which of the following languages is/are context-free?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- [latex]L_1\cap\overline{L_2}[/latex]: [latex]\overline{L_2}[/latex] need not be CFL [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] not always CFL.
- [latex]\overline{\overline{L_1}\cup\overline{L_2}}=L_1\cap L_2[/latex] (De Morgan) [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True
- [latex]L_2\cup\overline{L_2}=\Sigma^*[/latex], so the whole thing is [latex]\Sigma^*[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True
- [latex](L_1\cap L_2)\cup(\overline{L_1}\cap L_2)=L_2[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] CFL True

Answer: Options 2, 3 and 4

questions.text: In the context of compilers, which of the following is/are NOT an intermediate representation of the source program?
questions.solution:
Three address code, AST and CFG are all forms of the program used between front end and back end. The symbol table only stores information about names; it is not a representation of the program.

Answer: Symbol table

questions.text: Which of the following statement(s) is/are correct in the context of CPU scheduling?
questions.solution:
Checking each statement:
- Turnaround = completion [latex]-[/latex] arrival, which includes waiting time [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- The goal is to maximize throughput (and utilization), not minimize it [latex]\text{---}[/latex] FALSE.
- Round-robin only needs a time quantum, not burst lengths [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.
- Preemption needs a hardware timer interrupt [latex]\text{---}[/latex] TRUE.

Answer: Options 1, 3 and 4

questions.text:
Choose the correct choice(s) regarding the following proportional logic assertion S:

[latex]S: (( P \wedge Q) \rightarrow R) \rightarrow (( P \wedge Q) \rightarrow (Q \rightarrow R))[/latex]
questions.solution:
Simplify the consequent: [latex](P\wedge Q)\rightarrow(Q\rightarrow R)\equiv(P\wedge Q\wedge Q)\rightarrow R\equiv(P\wedge Q)\rightarrow R[/latex], which is exactly the antecedent.

So S has the form [latex]A\rightarrow A[/latex], which is always true.

Answer: S is a tautology; its antecedent is equivalent to its consequent

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: S  is neither a tautology nor a contradiction
The antecedent of S is logically equivalent to the consequent of S
